## Examining, Cleaning and Merging Data

```{r Examining Cleaning and Merging Data}
#checking data structures
str(nfl_plays20_21_22)

#checking head and tail of data
head(nfl_plays20_21_22)

#calculating descriptive statistics
#for all variables
#psych::describe(nfl_plays20_21_22)

#examing game-level data only
length(unique(nfl_plays20_21_22$game_id))
str(nfl_plays20_21_22$game_date)

#extracting year only from date and creating
#new variable for year
nfl_plays20_21_22$game_year <- as.numeric(substr(nfl_plays20_21_22$game_date, 
                                         start = 1, stop = 4))
#checking new variable
table(nfl_plays20_21_22[,c("game_date","game_year")])

#checking number of plays and games per year
summarytools::freq(nfl_plays20_21_22$game_year)

#2020 games only
nfl_plays20 <- subset(nfl_plays20_21_22, game_year == 2020)
length(unique(nfl_plays20$game_id))

#2021 games
nfl_plays21 <- subset(nfl_plays20_21_22, game_year == 2021)
length(unique(nfl_plays21$game_id))

#2022 games
nfl_plays22 <- subset(nfl_plays20_21_22, game_year == 2022)
length(unique(nfl_plays22$game_id))

#there are 509 total games in the dataset for 2020 and 2021, 
#with 240 games in the 2020 season and 269 games in the 2021 season
sum(length(unique(nfl_plays20$game_id)),
    length(unique(nfl_plays21$game_id)))

#removing 2022 games from dataset
#so only 2020 and 2021 games are left
nfl_plays20_21 <- subset(nfl_plays20_21_22, game_year == 2020 | game_year == 2021)

#reshaping data to only include game-level data
nfl_games_20_21 <- nfl_plays20_21 %>%
  dplyr::select(c("game_id","game_date","home_team","away_team","season_type",
                             "week","start_time","stadium","weather","temp",
                             "away_score","home_score","location",
                             "result","div_game","roof","surface","home_coach",
                             "away_coach","home_opening_kickoff")) %>%
  distinct()

#creating binary variable for home team won game
nfl_games_20_21$homewon <- ifelse(nfl_games_20_21$home_score > nfl_games_20_21$away_score,
                                  1,
                                  0)

#checking new variable
test <- data.frame(nfl_games_20_21$homewon,
                   nfl_games_20_21$home_score,
                   nfl_games_20_21$away_score)
head(test)


#creating binary variable for away team won game
nfl_games_20_21$awaywon <- ifelse(nfl_games_20_21$away_score > nfl_games_20_21$home_score,
                                  1,
                                  0)

#checking new variable
test <- data.frame(nfl_games_20_21$awaywon,
                   nfl_games_20_21$home_score,
                   nfl_games_20_21$away_score)
head(test)

#creating new temperature variable using string extraction
nfl_games_20_21$temp_new <- as.numeric(str_extract(substr(x = sub(".*Temp: ", "", 
                                                                  nfl_games_20_21$weather), 
                                                          start = 1, stop = 4), 
                                                   "\\d+"))

#checking new temperature variable
test <- nfl_games_20_21[,c("weather",
                           "temp_new")]

head(test)

#creating new humidity variable using string extraction
nfl_games_20_21$humidity <- as.numeric(str_extract(substr(x = sub(".*Humidity: ", "", 
                                                                  nfl_games_20_21$weather), 
                                                          start = 1, stop = 4), 
                                                   "\\d+"))

#checking new humidity variable
test <- nfl_games_20_21[,c("weather",
                           "temp_new",
                           "humidity")]


#merging in data for home and away teams for additional variables

#creating variables to match in datasets to merge in to
#original game-level data for 2020 and 2021
#with left join

#salary and elevation data table
nfl_salary_elevation_2020$home_team <- nfl_salary_elevation_2020$team_abbrv
nfl_salary_elevation_2020$away_team <- nfl_salary_elevation_2020$team_abbrv

#head coach data table
nfl_coach_data_2020$home_team <- nfl_coach_data_2020$Tm
nfl_coach_data_2020$away_team <- nfl_coach_data_2020$Tm

#need to merge in both salary and elevation data table 
#and head coach career length data table

#for home team and salary data table
nfl_games_20_21_merged_home <- merge(x = nfl_games_20_21,
                                y = nfl_salary_elevation_2020,
                                by = "home_team",
                                all.x = TRUE)

#for away team and salary data table
nfl_games_20_21_merged_away <- merge(nfl_games_20_21,
                                y = nfl_salary_elevation_2020,
                                by = "away_team",
                                all.x = TRUE)

#creating plots of coach data
ggplot(data= nfl_coach_data_2020, aes(x= reorder(Coach, W), y= W )) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity", width=0.5, fill="blue") +
    labs(title = "Coach Career Wins", x="Coach", y="Number of Wins") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + coord_flip()

ggplot(data= nfl_coach_data_2020, aes(x= reorder(Coach, L), y= L )) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity", width=0.5, fill="blue") +
    labs(title = "Coach Career Losses", x="Coach", y="Number of Losses") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + coord_flip()

#remove coaches fired during season to avoid duplicate Head Coaches
nfl_coach_data_2020_cleaned <- nfl_coach_data_2020[(!(nfl_coach_data_2020$Coach == "Dan Quinn") & 
                                                    !(nfl_coach_data_2020$Coach == "Matt Patricia") & 
                                                    !(nfl_coach_data_2020$Coach == "Bill O'Brien")),]

#print original and cleaned datasets
nfl_coach_data_2020
nfl_coach_data_2020_cleaned

#for home team and head coach data table
nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2 <- merge(nfl_games_20_21_merged_home,
                                y = nfl_coach_data_2020_cleaned,
                                by = "home_team",
                                all.x = TRUE)

#for away team and head coach data table
nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2 <- merge(nfl_games_20_21_merged_away,
                                y = nfl_coach_data_2020_cleaned,
                                by = "away_team",
                                all.x = TRUE)

#excluding non-relevant variable "Remark", "temp" and "roof" 
#with lots of missing values
nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2 <- subset(nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2, 
                                       select = -c(temp, roof, Remark))
nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2 <- subset(nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2, 
                                       select = -c(temp, roof, Remark))

#subsetting to only available data with listwise deletion
nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2 <- na.omit(nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2)
nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2 <- na.omit(nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2)

#writing final cleaned datasets to Excel files to share in case
#they are needed at a later date

#home wins dataset
write_excel_csv(nfl_games_20_21_merged_home2,
                file = "C:/Users/erlfo/Dropbox/Harvard Coursework/schooldocs/E109/GroupProject/NFL_games_coaches_salary_merged_homewins_2020_2021.xls")

#away wins dataset
write_excel_csv(nfl_games_20_21_merged_away2,
                file = "C:/Users/erlfo/Dropbox/Harvard Coursework/schooldocs/E109/GroupProject/NFL_games_coaches_salary_merged_awaywins_2020_2021.xls")

```

## Setting Up Data, Setting Outcome as Factor and Identifying All Features

```{r Setting Up Data, Factoring Outcome and Feature Identification}
#loading additional package to run
#stepwise logistic regression for
#selecting significant features
library(MASS)

#and load lime package to create explainer
#for black box models
library(lime)

#recoding outcomes as factor variables and
#renaming data to short name of NFL_home and NFL_away
data$homewon <- as.factor(data$homewon)

#examining frequencies for new factored outcome variable
freq(data$homewon)

#printing numeric variable names for regression equation
cat(names(Filter(is.numeric, data)), sep = " + ")

#week + temp + away_score + home_score + result + div_game + home_opening_kickoff + temp_new + humidity + signed + avg_age + active + dead + top_51_cap + cap_space...8 + total_cap + cap_space...10 + stad_elev_ft + G + W + L + T
```

## Fitting Logistic Regression and Identifying Optimal Models with Stepwise Regression

```{r Logistic Regression and Optimal Model Identification}
################### Logistic Regression ###########################

# Split data
set.seed(1234)
ind <- sample(2, nrow(data), replace = T, prob = c(0.8, 0.2))
trainNFL <- data[ind == 1,]
testNFL <- data[ind == 2,]

#summarizing data in training and testing dataset for predicting
#home team wins game
psych::describe(trainNFL)
psych::describe(testNFL)

# Logistic regression for numeric variables only
m <- glm(homewon ~ week + div_game + home_opening_kickoff + temp_new + humidity + avg_age + 
           active + stad_elev_ft + G + W, data = trainNFL, family = 'binomial'(link = "logit"))

summary(m)

#identify optimal model with forward and backwards stepwise models
model <- stepAIC(m, direction = "both", trace = F)

#print optimal model
summary(model)

#calculate odds ratios and confidence intervals for optimal model
round(exp(cbind(coef(model), confint(model))), digits = 2) 

# CM - train
p1 <- predict(model, trainNFL, type = 'response')
pred1 <- ifelse(p1 > 0.5, 1, 0)
table(Predicted = pred1, Actual = trainNFL$homewon)

#confusion matrix for training dataset
confusionMatrix(factor(pred1), factor(trainNFL$homewon), 
                positive = '1')

# CM - test
p2 <- predict(model, testNFL, type = 'response')
pred2 <- ifelse(p2 > 0.5, 1, 0)
table(Predicted = pred2, Actual = testNFL$homewon)

#confusion matrix for testing dataset
confusionMatrix(factor(pred2), factor(testNFL$homewon), 
                positive = '1')


# ROC for training dataset
r <- multiclass.roc(trainNFL$homewon, p1, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r1 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r1,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Train Data with Logistic Regression',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))


# ROC for testing dataset
r <- multiclass.roc(testNFL$homewon, p2, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r2 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r2,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Testing Data with Logistic Regression',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))

```

## Tree Models with Bagging, Random Forest Models and Extreme Gradient Boosted Models

```{r Tree, Random Forest and XGB Models}
################### Classification Trees##############################

# Bagging
set.seed(1234) 
cvcontrol <- trainControl(method="repeatedcv", 
                          number = 10,
                          repeats = 1,
                          allowParallel = TRUE)
set.seed(1234)
bag <- train(homewon ~ week + div_game + home_opening_kickoff + temp_new + humidity + avg_age + 
           active + stad_elev_ft + G + W, 
             data = trainNFL,
             method = "treebag",
             trControl = cvcontrol,
             importance = TRUE)

#print tree summary and variable importance plot
print(bag)
plot(varImp(bag))

#prediction in training dataset
p1 <- predict(bag, trainNFL, type = 'raw')
confusionMatrix(factor(p1), trainNFL$homewon, positive = '1')

#prediction in testing dataset
p2 <- predict(bag, testNFL, type = 'raw')
confusionMatrix(factor(p2), testNFL$homewon, positive = '1')


# ROC for training dataset
p1 <- predict(bag, trainNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(trainNFL$homewon, p1$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r1 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r1,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Train Data with Bagged Classification Tree',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))


# ROC for testing dataset
p2 <- predict(bag, testNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(testNFL$homewon, p2$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r2 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r2,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Testing Data with Bagged Classification Tree',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))


# Random forest model
set.seed(1234)
forest <- train(homewon ~ week + div_game + home_opening_kickoff + temp_new + humidity + avg_age + 
           active + stad_elev_ft + G + W, 
                data = trainNFL,
                method = "rf",
                trControl = cvcontrol,
                importance = TRUE)

#printing model summary and variable importance plot
print(forest)
plot(varImp(forest))

#predicting in training dataset
p1 <- predict(forest, trainNFL, type = 'prob')
p1 <- ifelse(p1[,2] > 0.4, 1, 0)
confusionMatrix(factor(p1), trainNFL$homewon, positive = '1')

#predicting in testing dataset
p2 <- predict(forest, testNFL, type = 'raw')
confusionMatrix(factor(p2), testNFL$homewon, positive = '1')

# ROC for training dataset
p1 <- predict(forest, trainNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(trainNFL$homewon, p1$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r1 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r1,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Train Data with Random Forest Model & 500 Trees',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))


# ROC for testing dataset
p2 <- predict(forest, testNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(testNFL$homewon, p2$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r2 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r2,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Testing Data with Random Forest Model & 500 Trees',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))

# Explain predictions, with only first 3 observations
# 5 variables and with the explained plot
explainer <- lime(testNFL[1:4,], forest, n_bins = 3)
explanation <- explain(x = testNFL[1:4,], 
                        explainer = explainer, 
                        n_features = 3,
                        n_labels = "1")
plot_features(explanation)

# Boosting
set.seed(1234)
boo <- train(homewon ~ week + div_game + home_opening_kickoff + temp_new + humidity + avg_age + 
           active + stad_elev_ft + G + W, 
             data = trainNFL,
             method = "xgbTree",   
             trControl = cvcontrol,
             tuneGrid = expand.grid(nrounds = 500,
                                    max_depth = 4,
                                    eta = 0.25,
                                    gamma = 1.0,
                                    colsample_bytree = 1,
                                    min_child_weight = 1,
                                    subsample = 1))

#printing model summary and variable importance plot
print(boo)
plot(varImp(boo))

#predicting in training dataset
p1 <- predict(boo, trainNFL, type = 'raw')
confusionMatrix(factor(p1), trainNFL$homewon, positive = '1')

#predicting in testing dataset
p2 <- predict(boo, testNFL, type = 'prob')
p2 <- ifelse(p2[,2] > 0.4, 1, 0)
confusionMatrix(factor(p2), testNFL$homewon, positive = '1')

# ROC for training dataset
p1 <- predict(boo, trainNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(trainNFL$homewon, p1$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r1 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r1,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Train Data w/ Extreme Gradient Boosting & 500 Rounds',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))


# ROC for testing dataset
p2 <- predict(boo, testNFL, type = 'prob')
r <- multiclass.roc(testNFL$homewon, p2$`1`, percent = TRUE)
roc <- r[['rocs']]
r2 <- roc[[1]]
plot.roc(r2,
         col = 'red',
         lwd = 5,
         main = 'ROC Curve for Testing Data w/ Extreme Gradient Boosting & 500 Rounds',
         cex.title = 0.8,
         print.auc = T,
         auc.polygon = T,
         grid = c(0.1, 0.2),
         grid.col = c('green', 'red'),
         max.auc.polygon = T,
         auc.polygon.col = 'lightblue',
         print.thres = "best",
         print.thres.best.method = "closest.topleft",
         print.auc.adj=c(0.5,8.5))
